page: Microsoft Azure D2a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. Virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs running on 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, yielding 4.0 GB per thread and adhering to the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio common to general-purpose cloud tiers. Hardware resources also include 54 GB of bundled local SSD storage, 32 MB of L3 cache, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, with no discrete GPU accelerators present.

Benchmark data displays a pronounced split between single-threaded efficiency and parallel capacity. In single-core evaluations, the instance performs well, achieving a top 25% ranking in stress-ng single-core tests and an average score of 1522.0 in Geekbench single-core testing. In contrast, aggregate multi-threaded metrics are restricted by the low core ceiling, placing stress-ng multi-core in the bottom 25% and Geekbench multi-core (1952.0) in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests indicate weak throughput, measuring 34.61 GB/sec on uncached reads and 24.14 GB/sec on uncached writes, while database operations and Redis SET throughput similarly fall into the lowest decile.

Because hardware resources are bounded by a single physical core and modest memory bandwidth, the instance prioritizes balanced entry-level resource allocation over dense compute or high-throughput I/O. It functions effectively for low-concurrency tasks, including microservices, dev/test environments, code compilation for modest projects, and basic static web serving, but it represents a clear architectural bottleneck for parallelized data processing or demanding production databases.
description: Microsoft Azure D2a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core with 2 threads, 8.0 GB of system memory, and 54 GB of local SSD storage, without GPU acceleration. The instance maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Benchmarks indicate competent single-core performance, ranking in the top 25% on stress-ng single-core evaluations and the middle 50% in Geekbench single-core testing. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics, memory bandwidth, and database tests place in the bottom 10% to 25%, limited by the low physical core count and memory bus constraints. The D2a_v4 provides a balanced compute-to-memory footprint for entry-level deployments, proving suitable for lightweight web serving, staging servers, basic continuous integration tasks, and low-traffic application backends that do not demand extensive parallel throughput or high I/O performance.
